newsitem.title: UK: Sterling sector welcomes second global bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Sterling sector welcomes second global bond issue.

text.p: The sterling international bond market made further strides on Friday with the launch of the second global bond which will be sold into Asia, Europe and the U.S.

The U.S. government sponsored Federal Home Loan Banks issued a 300 million stg June 2002 global bond. The deal will be priced to yield 10 basis points over the 7.0 percent June 2002 gilt via Goldman Sachs.

"It is a significant transaction and reflects the current international focus on sterling," a Goldman Sachs syndicate official told Reuters. "The deal has seen extremely good demand and a strong take-up from investors in Britain and Asia."

The sterling Eurobond sector has flourished on the back of a robust pound and the relatively high yields available in Britain. Sterling is also perceived as a "safe haven" currency, unlikely to join the European economic and monetary union single currency at the outset.
"The foreign focus on sterling will continue as it remains a strong currency and yields are attractive relative to core European markets," the syndicate head at a British bank said.
"Spreads of 150 basis points or more over Germany will remain attractive to international investors. We have seen many increase their portfolio weighting of sterling paper."
FHLB is rated triple-A by both Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's Corp and consists of 12 individual banks that specialise in residential housing finance.
The first sterling-denominated global bond was launched for the U.S. national mortgage association Fannie Mae on February 11, and was snapped up by international investors.
The distribution of sales was 47 percent into Britain, 20 percent into Asia, 18 percent into Continental Europe and 15 percent into the U.S.

Fannie Mae's 1.0 billion stg June 2002 deal has tightened from a launch spread of 10 basis points over the 7.0 percent gilt due June 2002, to a bid of 7.5 b.p over at 1100 GMT on Friday, dealers said.
Joint lead managers for that transaction were BZW and Merrill Lynch.
